what: The nine scheduler events (FailedScheduling and the eight Scheduled rows) sit at their chronological places among the kubelet/controller events: 'Scheduled pod/cache-67765b96c6-zrpfn' (12m) comes after the three 13m rows, and the Scheduled rows for the checkout-api, inventory-sync and report-worker pods are scattered through the 12m block.
why: default-scheduler records events through events.k8s.io/v1, so the core/v1 object a real API server returns has eventTime set and lastTimestamp: null. kubectl sorts --sort-by client-side on the row objects and puts null values first, so a real cluster lists all nine scheduler events at the top, whatever their LAST SEEN, and only then the rest in time order. The interleaving means the served Event objects carry a non-null lastTimestamp for scheduler events. No step prints the raw Event objects, so this rests on how the scheduler and kubectl behave, not on a contradiction inside the record.
